A handle for a freed slot mismatches on the generation bump and can never pass again — except after 2^32 frees of that one slot (defined unsigned wrap; effectively unreachable, documented here as the one case the generation scheme does not rule out).

symbols.summary: Destroy every live element; every handle becomes stale; the capacity is unchanged and the pool is immediately reusable. O(capacity), no allocation. (Reset-per-frame workloads should use ArenaPool<T> instead — its reset() is O(inUse) and has no free-list bookkeeping.)

symbols.name: laige::Pool::stats
symbols.summary: Accounting snapshot (PRD §10.4). bytesCapacity is the whole backing store (element slots + per-slot generation/alive/free-list bookkeeping); bytesInUse is the element footprint of live elements.

symbols.name: laige::Prng
symbols.summary: Prng — deterministic xorshift128+ with seeded, per-substream derivation (M0-CORE-06; contract preamble above; full API doc: docs/api/prng.md)

symbols.name: laige::Prng::kSplitmix64Increment
symbols.summary: splitmix64 increment (Marsaglia's golden-ratio odd constant): the step between successive splitmix64 inputs and between substream seeds.

symbols.name: laige::Prng::kMixMultiplierA
symbols.summary: splitmix64 mixing multipliers (Stafford 2018).

symbols.name: laige::Prng::kFloat01Unit
symbols.summary: next_float01() resolution: one value is 2^-24 (24 mantissa bits).

symbols.name: laige::Prng::Prng
symbols.signature: explicit Prng(std::uint64_t seed) : seed_(seed), s0_(0), s1_(0)
symbols.summary: Construct the master stream for `seed`. The state is nonzero for every seed (splitmix64 is a bijection; see the preamble).

symbols.name: laige::Prng::next_u64
symbols.summary: One stream draw: the xorshift128+ output; advances the state.

symbols.name: laige::Prng::next_range
symbols.summary: Uniform value in [min, max) (max - min must be in [1, 2^32 - 1]). Unbiased (Lemire reduction with rejection); expected < 2 draws. `min >= max` is a debug assert (documented UB in release).

symbols.name: laige::Prng::next_float01
symbols.summary: Uniform value in [0, 1) at 24-bit resolution: exactly k * 2^-24 for an integer k in [0, 2^24). Never 1.0; 0.0 with probability 2^-24.

symbols.name: laige::Prng::seed
symbols.summary: The seed this stream was constructed from (save/replay identity, PRD §10.3; M1-DET-03 hashes this together with the substream id).

symbols.name: laige::Prng::substream
symbols.summary: A substream of this stream's seed: deriveSubstream(seed(), id). Independent stream position; id 0 == the master stream.

symbols.name: laige::Prng::deriveSubstream
symbols.signature: static Prng deriveSubstream(std::uint64_t seed, std::uint32_t id)
symbols.summary: Substream derivation (documented hash, see the preamble): Prng(seed + id * kSplitmix64Increment). Composes: deriveSubstream(deriveSubstream(seed, i), j) == deriveSubstream(seed, i+j).

symbols.summary: Seed-to-state mapping (documented in the preamble). Exposed for determinism verification and M1 save/replay: a saved stream is (seed, part1, part2) and restores by seedState + stepState calls.

symbols.signature: static void stepState(std::uint64_t& part1, std::uint64_t& part2)
symbols.summary: One transition step on a raw state (see the preamble). Exposed for determinism verification (the PrngPeriod suite reconstructs the state map over GF(2) from this) and M1 save/replay.

symbols.summary: splitmix64 (Stafford 2018) — seeding-only; a bijection of u64.

The signature stays distinct from the value constructor even when T and E are the same type, which keeps the class well-formed on all conforming compilers (MSVC rejects two member declarations with identical parameter lists).

symbols.name: laige::sim::SimMath::length
symbols.summary: length is exactly sqrt(x*x + y*y): two muls, one add, one correctly-rounded sqrt, in that order. fp32_pinned: the pinned -ffp-contract=off keeps x*x + y*y from FMA-contraction, which would round once and change the result. fpx16_16: the squarings and the sum are saturating Q16.16 ops, so length is accurate while x*x + y*y stays inside the Q16.16 range (|v| ≲ 181.02 per component; beyond that the result saturates — defined, deterministic, documented in fpx16_16.h and docs/api/sim_math.md).

The zero vector is defined to normalize to the zero vector (SimMath never injects NaN from a zero-length input; the fixed-point backend has no NaN at all). NaN/inf components propagate per the backend's policy (fp32_pinned: IEEE — an infinite vector can normalize to NaN components).
